title: Part 1: What to Expect When You’re Expecting (the Mueller Report)

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上，现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The Democratic National Committee is trying to solve a spy mystery.
sentences.zh: 民主党全国委员会正试图解开一个间谍谜团。

sentences.en: It began before dawn
sentences.zh: 事情发生在周六

sentences.en: Saturday when five intruders were captured by police inside the offices of the committee in Washington.
sentences.zh: 黎明前，五名闯入者在华盛顿的委员会办公室内被警方逮捕。

sentences.en: Throughout U.S.
sentences.zh: 纵观美国

sentences.en: history.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: The tangled relationship between an Arkansas land deal, a savings and loan, and Hillary Rodham Clinton's former law firm is again under scrutiny today.
sentences.zh: 阿肯色州的一笔土地交易、一家储贷机构与希拉里·罗德姆·克林顿的前律师事务所之间错综复杂的关系，今天再次受到审视。

sentences.en: There have only been a handful of investigations into possible criminal conduct by a sitting president.
sentences.zh: 针对在任总统可能存在的犯罪行为，历史上仅有少数几次调查。

sentences.en: I did not have sexual relations with that woman.
sentences.zh: 我没有和那个女人发生性关系。

sentences.en: Mr. Nixon says emphatically that the White House is in no way involved in the burglary and bugging of the Democratic headquarters, and he'll have no further comment on that matter.
sentences.zh: 尼克松先生强调，白宫绝未参与民主党总部的入室盗窃和窃听事件，他对此事不会再发表任何评论。

sentences.en: And each time...
sentences.zh: 而每一次……

sentences.en: Attorney General Klein deed plays a comprehensive, unbiased investigation of the break-in at
sentences.zh: 司法部长克莱恩·迪德（Klein）对6月份发生在

sentences.en: Democratic National Committee headquarters on June...
sentences.zh: 民主党全国委员会总部的入室盗窃案进行了全面、公正的调查……

sentences.en: An outside investigator has been appointed.
sentences.zh: 一名外部调查员已被任命。

sentences.en: Whitewater counsel Kenneth Starr has been granted permission to expand his investigation.
sentences.zh: 白水事件特别检察官肯尼斯·斯塔尔已获准扩大他的调查范围。

sentences.en: And that investigator has to follow a set of guidelines, a set of rules to ensure they are both independent and accountable.
sentences.zh: 而且那位调查员必须遵循一套准则，一套确保他们既独立又负责的规则。

sentences.en: This is a sacred process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个神圣的过程。

sentences.en: This is not a witch hunt.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场政治迫害。

sentences.en: And then, after each of these investigations, those guidelines have changed in response to the
sentences.zh: 然后，在每一次调查之后，这些准则都会根据

sentences.en: perceived flaws or excesses of the most recent investigation in an attempt to improve them.
sentences.zh: 最近一次调查中被认为存在的缺陷或过激行为进行修改，以试图完善它们。

sentences.en: Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein is announcing the appointment of a special counsel...
sentences.zh: 副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦宣布任命一名特别检察官……

sentences.en: Now, the latest set of rules...
sentences.zh: 现在，最新的一套规则……

sentences.en: Former FBI Director Robert Mueller will now lead the investigation...
sentences.zh: 前联邦调查局局长罗伯特·穆勒将领导这项调查……

sentences.en: ...are being really tested for the first time, as special counsel Robert Mueller prepares to release his report later this month.
sentences.zh: ……正受到真正的考验，因为特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒准备在本月晚些时候发布他的报告。

sentences.en: Just got on.
sentences.zh: 刚上线。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: It's really great to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Hey, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Ditto.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: So, we wanted to sit down with Neil Codial, because he's the person who wrote those rules.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们想和尼尔·卡蒂亚尔（Neal Katyal）坐下来谈谈，因为他就是制定这些规则的人。

sentences.en: It's Monday, March 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月4日，星期一。

sentences.en: Shall we start?
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Neil, from your very informed point of view, what do you expect this report to actually look like?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，从你非常专业的角度来看，你认为这份报告实际上会是什么样子？

sentences.en: So, the first report that Mueller will send to the Attorney General is supposed to be a summary of the investigation.
sentences.zh: 穆勒提交给司法部长的第一份报告应该是调查的摘要。

sentences.en: And it's supposed to detail, you know, the roads taken, the roads not taken, reasons why.
sentences.zh: 它应该详细说明，你知道，走过的路，没走的路，以及原因。

sentences.en: And then there's a second report, and that is the report that the
sentences.zh: 然后是第二份报告，那份报告是

sentences.en: Attorney General, William Barr, is going to give to the Congress.
sentences.zh: 司法部长威廉·巴尔将提交给国会的报告。

sentences.en: I don't think that the special counsel regulations envision the two reports to look the same.
sentences.zh: 我不认为特别检察官条例设想这两份报告看起来是一样的。

sentences.en: And why do you say think?
sentences.zh: 为什么你说“认为”？

sentences.en: Having written these rules, don't you know exactly what they envision?
sentences.zh: 既然是你写的这些规则，难道你不知道它们确切的设想是什么吗？

sentences.en: I think the best way of thinking about the special counsel regulations is to think about it a little bit, and not to sound grandiose, but like a constitution.
sentences.zh: 我认为思考特别检察官条例的最好方式，是把它看作——这听起来可能有点夸张——类似于宪法的东西。

sentences.en: You can't anticipate all of the crises that are going to happen in the years to come in a dynamic republic.
sentences.zh: 在一个充满活力的共和国里，你无法预见未来几年将要发生的所有危机。

sentences.en: And so, you don't have hard and fast rules.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不会有死板的硬性规定。

sentences.en: You have some rules, and then you have the spirit and the animating principles behind them.
sentences.zh: 你有一些规则，然后你还有这些规则背后的精神和核心原则。

sentences.en: The animating focus of the special counsel regulations is to restore what it calls public confidence in the integrity of the process.
sentences.zh: 特别检察官条例的核心重点是恢复它所说的公众对程序公正性的信心。

sentences.en: And then reasoning backward from that, what's the best thing I could do as Attorney General when I'm writing this report
sentences.zh: 然后反过来推导，作为司法部长，我在撰写这份报告时能做的最好的事情是什么，

sentences.en: to help facilitate that public confidence in the administration of justice?
sentences.zh: 以帮助促进公众对司法行政的信心？

sentences.en: If the crime is, you know, something very serious of national security concern, like potential collusion with Russia, more is going to be important.
sentences.zh: 如果犯罪涉及非常严重的国家安全问题，比如与俄罗斯潜在的勾结，那么更多的信息将非常重要。

sentences.en: If the crime is something that's much more minor, less information is required.
sentences.zh: 如果犯罪性质轻微得多，那么所需的信息就较少。

sentences.en: And to me, that means that more information is required rather than less when you're dealing with the highest level of our government, the president of the United States,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这意味着当你处理我们政府最高层，即美国总统，

sentences.en: and potential wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 以及潜在的不当行为时，需要更多的信息，而不是更少。

sentences.en: So you're saying the guidelines will encourage the Attorney General to give something quite comprehensive to Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，这些准则将鼓励司法部长向国会提供相当全面的内容。

sentences.en: I don't want to say it's quite comprehensive.
sentences.zh: 我不想说它“相当全面”。

sentences.en: The regulations say that the Attorney General is supposed to tell Congress the fact that the investigations concluded, some reasons why,
sentences.zh: 条例规定，司法部长应该告诉国会调查已经结束的事实，说明一些原因，

sentences.en: and to detail any instances in which the Attorney General or the Attorney General's predecessors,
sentences.zh: 并详细说明司法部长或司法部长的继任者，

sentences.en: like Whitaker or Rod Rosenstein, who was the acting Attorney General, any instances in which they said no to Mueller.
sentences.zh: 比如惠特克或担任代理司法部长的罗德·罗森斯坦，在哪些情况下他们对穆勒说了“不”。

sentences.en: Now, Barr could certainly go further and provide a lot of detail.
sentences.zh: 当然，巴尔可以更进一步，提供大量细节。

sentences.en: I think if Mueller decides not to prosecute X, despite there being some evidence, or to prosecute
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果穆勒决定不对某人提起诉讼，尽管有一些证据，或者决定起诉

sentences.en: Y, I think those are the types of things that have to be explained in this report from Barr to Congress.
sentences.zh: 某人，我认为这些就是巴尔提交给国会的报告中必须解释的事情。

sentences.en: But are we going to get something like the Star Report or the 9-11 report, you know, that's going to be a big coffee table document?
sentences.zh: 但我们能得到像《斯塔尔报告》或《9/11调查报告》那样的大部头文件吗？

sentences.en: You know, I don't think we'll see that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不认为我们会看到那样的情况。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why aren't we going to get a coffee table size version of this?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们得不到一个大部头版本的报告？

sentences.en: I think that's what many of us have been expecting.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是我们许多人所期待的。

sentences.en: Why isn't a full report from Mueller what goes to Congress rather than the AG's report on the report?
sentences.zh: 为什么提交给国会的不是穆勒的完整报告，而是司法部长关于报告的报告？

sentences.en: When we wrote the special counsel regulations, we weren't writing them in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 当我们撰写特别检察官条例时，我们并不是在真空中撰写的。

sentences.en: We were writing them after many, many pages dumped on Congress in the Ken Starr report about Monica Lewinsky and
sentences.zh: 我们是在肯·斯塔尔关于莫妮卡·莱温斯基和

sentences.en: Whitewater.
sentences.zh: 白水事件的报告中，向国会倾倒了大量页面之后撰写的。

sentences.en: And that, I think, should concern all Americans, that you have a prosecutor really, I think, impinching on some of the most sensitive privacy concerns that human beings have.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这应该引起所有美国人的担忧，即检察官真的在侵犯人类最敏感的一些隐私问题。

sentences.en: And so the requirements in the special counsel regulations are not written the way they were in the Independent
sentences.zh: 因此，特别检察官条例中的要求，并没有像《独立检察官法》那样，

sentences.en: Counsel Act to provide every piece of information that was a concern.
sentences.zh: 要求提供每一条令人担忧的信息。

sentences.en: On the other side was also the need for public confidence.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，也需要考虑公众的信心。

sentences.en: And so it's going to depend on the case.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于具体案件。

sentences.en: In a case in which you're dealing with, you know, private consenting activity among adults, you know, you're not going to really
sentences.zh: 在处理成年人之间私下自愿行为的案件中，你真的

sentences.en: want to have the same level of detail as when you're talking about, say, collusion with Russia.
sentences.zh: 不会想要像谈论，比如说，与俄罗斯勾结时那样详尽的细节。

sentences.en: And I think maybe to just take a step back and understand what's going on, why is all this written this way?
sentences.zh: 我想也许退一步来理解正在发生的事情，为什么这一切要这样写？

sentences.en: It's written this way because of the kind of oldest fear that democracies have, which is who's going to guard the guardians?
sentences.zh: 这样写是因为民主国家最古老的恐惧，即“谁来监督监督者”？

sentences.en: Or if you are a Dr. Seuss fan, who's going to be the bee watcher to the bee watcher watcher and so on?
sentences.zh: 或者如果你是苏斯博士的粉丝，谁来监督监督监督者的人，以此类推？

sentences.en: And here, the idea is that the attorney general is supervising this investigation into the president, which is remarkable because who appoints the attorney general?
sentences.zh: 在这里，其理念是司法部长正在监督这项针对总统的调查，这很引人注目，因为谁任命司法部长？

sentences.en: The president.
sentences.zh: 总统。

sentences.en: And the way to try and deal with that hornet's nest is to say, look, we can't take the attorney general out of the prosecutorial system.
sentences.zh: 而处理这个马蜂窝的方法是说，看，我们不能把司法部长从检察系统中剔除。

sentences.en: That's what our constitution requires.
sentences.zh: 这是我们宪法的要求。

sentences.en: But we can make sure that sunlight is shed upon the attorney general's actions when supervising that special counsel.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以确保司法部长在监督特别检察官时的行为能够被阳光照亮。

sentences.en: And so that's why the reporting requirement exists.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么存在报告要求的原因。

sentences.en: And that's why it can't be that it's simply be a one line, like we're closing the investigation and nothing else.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它不能仅仅是一行字，比如“我们正在结束调查”，而没有其他内容。

sentences.en: There's really got to be an outline of the actions and the reasons for them.
sentences.zh: 确实必须有一个行动大纲及其背后的原因。

sentences.en: So given that the attorney general is a presidential nominee, works for the man who is under investigation,
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于司法部长是总统提名的，为正在接受调查的人工作，

sentences.en: why should we trust that this person will follow the sort of broad outlines that you're describing rather than firm rules that explicitly say what must happen?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们应该相信这个人会遵循你所描述的那种广泛大纲，而不是明确规定必须发生什么的硬性规则？

sentences.en: In our constitutional system, there really is no way to force an attorney general to do something that he doesn't want to do when it comes to a special counsel.
sentences.zh: 在我们的宪政体制中，当涉及到特别检察官时，确实没有办法强迫司法部长做他不想做的事情。

sentences.en: Because after all, the special counsel regulations are themselves just the creation of the attorney general.
sentences.zh: 因为毕竟，特别检察官条例本身就是司法部长制定的。

sentences.en: They can be repealed by an attorney general at any time.
sentences.zh: 司法部长随时可以废除它们。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: And so the idea behind these special counsel regulations is to just make it really difficult for an attorney general, a willful one, to interfere with an investigation.
sentences.zh: 所以这些特别检察官条例背后的理念，只是为了让司法部长，一个任性的司法部长，很难干预调查。

sentences.en: And so you outline the kind of concerns that an attorney general has to consider, like public confidence in the administration of justice.
sentences.zh: 因此，你列出了司法部长必须考虑的各种担忧，比如公众对司法行政的信心。

sentences.en: And then you hope for an attorney general and a confirmation process that ensures an attorney general whose character is such that the right thing will be done.
sentences.zh: 然后你寄希望于司法部长和确认程序，确保司法部长的品格能够保证做正确的事。

sentences.en: We certainly anticipated that there'd be attorneys general who would act and, you know, be appointed in a political process.
sentences.zh: 我们当然预料到会有司法部长在政治进程中采取行动并被任命。

sentences.en: After all, we were all very well aware that, you know, Bobby Kennedy was John F.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我们都很清楚，你知道，鲍比·肯尼迪是约翰·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy's attorney general.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪的司法部长。

sentences.en: So it's not as if we were unaware of the possibility of political attorneys general or ones who had family relationships and the like.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是我们不知道政治性司法部长或有家庭关系等情况的可能性。

sentences.en: But at the same time, in our constitutional system, there's no way to remove the attorney general from the process.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在我们的宪政体制中，没有办法将司法部长从这个过程中移除。

sentences.en: And so all we could do was try and shed sunlight into the decisions made by the attorney general.
sentences.zh: 所以我们能做的就是尝试将阳光照进司法部长所做的决定中。

sentences.en: So let's talk about how the sunlight process works.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们谈谈阳光程序是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Once the AG report goes to Congress, what is in place to be sure that there is sunlight?
sentences.zh: 一旦司法部长的报告提交给国会，有什么机制来确保有阳光？

sentences.en: The special counsel regulations actually require the attorney general report to go not just to the majority in Congress, but also to the minority party.
sentences.zh: 特别检察官条例实际上要求司法部长的报告不仅要提交给国会多数党，还要提交给少数党。

sentences.en: Here, it doesn't matter because there is now a Democratic or cross-party House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 在这里，这无关紧要，因为现在众议院是民主党控制的，或者是跨党派的。

sentences.en: But had this happened a year ago or six months ago, we wouldn't have been able to say that.
sentences.zh: 但如果这种情况发生在一年或六个月前，我们就不能这么说了。

sentences.en: So that's step one.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一步。

sentences.en: Step two is, in the special counsel regulations, is a provision for public disclosure of the report, not just to
sentences.zh: 第二步是，在特别检察官条例中，有一项关于报告公开披露的条款，不仅是向

sentences.en: Congress, but to the American people.
sentences.zh: 国会，也是向美国人民公开。

sentences.en: So in part nine of the regulations, it says the attorney general is to make a determination that the public interest would be served by public release of the documents.
sentences.zh: 因此，在条例的第九部分中，它说司法部长要做出决定，即公开披露这些文件是否符合公共利益。

sentences.en: Now, it's clear to say there are applicable legal restrictions, you know, so grand jury information can't ordinarily be released to the public.
sentences.zh: 现在，很明显，存在适用的法律限制，你知道，大陪审团的信息通常不能向公众发布。

sentences.en: But that's the way it would work, as the attorney general would review the report that he's written and say, yeah, I think this should be made public,
sentences.zh: 但这就是它的运作方式，司法部长会审查他所写的报告，并说，是的，我认为这应该公开，

sentences.en: or maybe there'll be some redactions and then be made public.
sentences.zh: 或者也许会有一些删减，然后公开。

sentences.en: And what do you expect Congress to do with this report?
sentences.zh: 你期望国会对这份报告做什么？

sentences.en: And is that part of what you envisioned in your guidelines?
sentences.zh: 这是你在准则中设想的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I think the answer to that really does turn on how much information is given to Congress and does it look like a cover-up?
sentences.zh: 我认为这个问题的答案确实取决于提供给国会多少信息，以及它看起来是否像掩盖真相？

sentences.en: If it does, if there's stuff that Barr is not providing that looks really suspicious, then I expect Congress to start subpoenaing Mueller,
sentences.zh: 如果确实如此，如果巴尔没有提供的东西看起来非常可疑，那么我预计国会将开始传唤穆勒、

sentences.en: Mueller's team, the documents they've uncovered, and who knows what else to try and get at what actually happened and find the truth out.
sentences.zh: 穆勒的团队、他们发现的文件，以及谁知道还有什么，以试图弄清到底发生了什么并找出真相。

sentences.en: Can you give me an example of what that might look like?
sentences.zh: 你能给我举个例子说明那可能是什么样子吗？

sentences.en: What Congress might see in the report that the attorney general sends that would cause lawmakers to say, wait a minute, something's amiss.
sentences.zh: 国会在司法部长发送的报告中可能会看到什么，从而导致立法者说，“等一下，有什么不对劲。”

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么事？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So think about the firing of Jim Comey, the FBI director.
sentences.zh: 想想解雇联邦调查局局长吉姆·科米这件事。

sentences.en: At first, the president's statement was, you know, I did it because Jim Comey was unfair to Hillary Clinton in criticizing her.
sentences.zh: 起初，总统的声明是，你知道，我这样做是因为吉姆·科米在批评希拉里·克林顿时对她不公平。

sentences.en: You know, when that story fell apart, the president ultimately admitted to Lester Holt, I did it because of Russia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当那个故事破灭时，总统最终向莱斯特·霍尔特承认，我这样做是因为俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And that's what led to this whole obstruction of justice investigation.
sentences.zh: 而这正是导致整个妨碍司法调查的原因。

sentences.en: Can you fire the FBI director because you're upset that he's investigating you?
sentences.zh: 你可以因为你不高兴他在调查你而解雇联邦调查局局长吗？

sentences.en: That's something
sentences.zh: 那是

sentences.en: Mueller's investigating.
sentences.zh: 穆勒正在调查的事情。

sentences.en: Suppose Barr writes a report to Congress that says, obstruction of justice, we decided not to indict the president, period.
sentences.zh: 假设巴尔写了一份报告给国会，说：“妨碍司法，我们决定不起诉总统，句号。”

sentences.en: Doesn't explain why.
sentences.zh: 没有解释原因。

sentences.en: There would then be two possible big buckets of reasons why that decision could be made.
sentences.zh: 那么做出这个决定可能有两大类原因。

sentences.en: One is the facts just weren't there.
sentences.zh: 一是事实根本不存在。

sentences.en: Maybe they found that Trump didn't have a corrupt intent.
sentences.zh: 也许他们发现特朗普没有腐败意图。

sentences.en: Maybe he wanted to do it for other reasons.
sentences.zh: 也许他有其他理由才这么做。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But the second bucket is what Bill Barr wrote in his 19-page memo to Trump when he was, you know, some people say campaigning for the job or
sentences.zh: 但第二个“桶”就是比尔·巴尔在写给特朗普的那份19页备忘录中所提到的内容，当时他，你知道的，有些人说是为了竞选这个职位，或者

sentences.en: whatever, which is to adopt a really pretty ridiculous legal theory, which was the president
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，也就是采用了一种非常荒谬的法律理论，即总统

sentences.en: can't obstruct justice when he fires a cabinet official because, after all, presidents can fire cabinet officials for any reason.
sentences.zh: 在解雇内阁官员时不能妨碍司法公正，因为毕竟总统可以以任何理由解雇内阁官员。

sentences.en: That's generally right, but you can't have a kind of corrupt motive.
sentences.zh: 这通常是对的，但你不能有某种腐败的动机。

sentences.en: It's just like, you know, I have a laptop and I can throw it into the river or set it on fire if I want.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，我有一台笔记本电脑，如果我想的话，我可以把它扔进河里或者把它烧掉。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: I have the right to do that.
sentences.zh: 我有权这样做。

sentences.en: But if I know the FBI is coming and looking for the laptop and they have a warrant, I can't go do those things.
sentences.zh: 但如果我知道联邦调查局要来搜查这台笔记本电脑，而且他们有搜查令，我就不能去干这些事了。

sentences.en: So same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以是一样的道理。

sentences.en: The president can fire a cabinet rank official generally, but he can't do it in order to obstruct justice.
sentences.zh: 总统通常可以解雇内阁级别的官员，但他不能为了妨碍司法公正而这样做。

sentences.en: And so if the Barr memo didn't explain why to Congress he wasn't pursuing a prosecution,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果巴尔的备忘录没有向国会解释他为什么不进行起诉，

sentences.en: then absolutely that would be something in which it would raise every investigator's hackles and we'd have to get to the bottom of it.
sentences.zh: 那么这绝对会引起每一位调查人员的警觉，我们必须查个水落石出。

sentences.en: Let me give you another example.
sentences.zh: 让我再给你举个例子。

sentences.en: Suppose that Barr says, you know, I'm not indicting the president for collusion with Russia.
sentences.zh: 假设巴尔说，你知道，我不会因为与俄罗斯勾结而起诉总统。

sentences.en: Doesn't explain why.
sentences.zh: 没有解释原因。

sentences.en: Again, there's two possible reasons.
sentences.zh: 同样，有两个可能的原因。

sentences.en: One is the facts aren't there.
sentences.zh: 一个是事实依据不足。

sentences.en: The other is under some of these old Justice Department opinions, a sitting president can't be indicted.
sentences.zh: 另一个是根据司法部的一些旧观点，在任总统不能被起诉。

sentences.en: If Barr doesn't tell which, absolutely Congress and perhaps other investigators need to subpoena the documents to find out what actually happened here.
sentences.zh: 如果巴尔不说明是哪种情况，国会以及其他调查人员绝对需要传唤相关文件，以查明这里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They should not just have to guess at the reasoning behind the attorney general's decision.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该只能去猜测司法部长决定背后的理由。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we've all been focused so much on the Mueller report and the Barr report, and those are undoubtedly important.
sentences.zh: 我们大家都太关注穆勒报告和巴尔报告了，这些无疑是很重要的。

sentences.en: But I think one thing to think about is how the Mueller and Barr reports set up a springboard to further investigations.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一点值得思考，那就是穆勒和巴尔的报告是如何为进一步的调查搭建跳板的。

sentences.en: Now there are multiple investigators.
sentences.zh: 现在有多个调查方。

sentences.en: There's the democratically controlled House of
sentences.zh: 有民主党控制的众议院，

sentences.en: Representatives and multiple committees therein.
sentences.zh: 以及其中的多个委员会。

sentences.en: There's the Southern District of New York and the campaign finance investigation they're undertaking, as well as the investigation into the Trump organization.
sentences.zh: 有纽约南区联邦检察官办公室，他们正在进行竞选财务调查，以及对特朗普集团的调查。

sentences.en: And there are state attorneys general.
sentences.zh: 还有各州的司法部长。

sentences.en: So when Barr and Mueller write their reports, their audience is not simply Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以当巴尔和穆勒撰写报告时，他们的受众不仅仅是国会。

sentences.en: And it's not perhaps even just the American people.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能不仅仅是美国人民。

sentences.en: It's also these other investigators.
sentences.zh: 还有这些其他的调查人员。

sentences.en: If they don't do a good enough job at explaining what they've done, and it looks like a coverup, that's going to fuel the fire of these other investigations.
sentences.zh: 如果他们解释得不够充分，看起来像是在掩盖事实，那只会给这些调查火上浇油。

sentences.en: Then you're going to have a kind of hydra of investigations with multiple different nodes.
sentences.zh: 到时候你就会看到一种多节点的“九头蛇”式调查。

sentences.en: And that's going to, I think, actually become even more worrisome for Trump than the current kind of single focus that we've had for many of the last months.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这实际上会比我们过去几个月所经历的那种单一焦点，让特朗普感到更加担忧。

sentences.en: So the less information that's in it, the more likely these other investigations just multiply and intensify.
sentences.zh: 所以报告里的信息越少，这些其他调查就越有可能成倍增加并愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Donald Trump has to be worried about winning the battle and losing the war.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普必须担心赢了战斗却输了战争。

sentences.en: That is, is getting a short report that maybe sides with him and maybe sides with him in a brief way because
sentences.zh: 也就是说，得到一份简短的、可能偏袒他的报告，而且是以一种草率的方式偏袒他，因为

sentences.en: that, more than anything, is going to raise the suspicions of Congress, of federal prosecutors
sentences.zh: 这比什么都更能引起国会、联邦检察官

sentences.en: and other offices, and state attorneys general, and ultimately the suspicions of the American public.
sentences.zh: 以及其他办公室、州司法部长，最终是美国公众的怀疑。

sentences.en: So counterintuitively, I mean, very counterintuitively, the best thing for President Trump might be for
sentences.zh: 所以反直觉的是，我是说，非常反直觉的是，对特朗普总统来说最好的事情，可能反而是

sentences.en: Congress to receive not a short, nothing much there to report Mueller report, but a fairly comprehensive, somewhat damning, but not overwhelmingly so, report.
sentences.zh: 国会收到的不是一份简短的、没什么内容的穆勒报告，而是一份相当全面、有些定罪意味，但又不至于压倒性的报告。

sentences.en: That's a beautiful summary.
sentences.zh: 总结得太好了。

sentences.en: And I know it sounds counterintuitive, but in some ways, when you have that kind of very
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很反直觉，但在某种程度上，当你拥有那种非常

sentences.en: serious watchdog, it keeps you on your toes, to be absolutely honest, but also really reassures the American public that there isn't some shenanigan going on.
sentences.zh: 严肃的监督者时，说实话，这会让你保持警惕，同时也确实能让美国公众放心，不会有什么猫腻发生。

sentences.en: And so sometimes the best protection you can have is actually to have a vigorous investigator.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候你能拥有的最好保护，其实就是有一位强有力的调查者。

sentences.en: Obviously, Donald Trump has been afraid of that from the start.
sentences.zh: 显然，唐纳德·特朗普从一开始就害怕这一点。

sentences.en: And the lingering question I think all Americans have is why.
sentences.zh: 而我认为所有美国人心中挥之不去的问题是：为什么？

sentences.en: Are you concerned at all that if, if and when this report moves into this kind of,
sentences.zh: 你是否担心，如果，当这份报告演变成你所说的这种“九头蛇”式、多头模式时，

sentences.en: as you called it, HYDRA, many-headed model, that it also inherently kind of inevitably becomes more partisan?
sentences.zh: 它是否也会不可避免地变得更加党派化？

sentences.en: And therefore, it's more open to criticism, more open to division, and that we might be better served if it were all completed through the process of a special counsel?
sentences.zh: 因此，它更容易受到批评，更容易导致分裂，如果我们通过特别检察官的程序来完成这一切，会不会效果更好？

sentences.en: I think when we wrote the special counsel regulations, we really hoped that the special counsel would be
sentences.zh: 我认为当我们起草特别检察官条例时，我们确实希望特别检察官能成为

sentences.en: the primary driver of the investigation, because that would be someone who was chosen for their unimpeachable integrity.
sentences.zh: 调查的主要推动者，因为那将是一个因其无可挑剔的正直品质而被选中的人。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right to say, as the investigation morphs into a variety of different nodes, you can't guarantee that same level of stature, of independence, of non-partisanship,
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确，随着调查演变成各种不同的节点，你无法保证同样水平的地位、独立性和非党派性，

sentences.en: and things do become more political.
sentences.zh: 事情确实会变得更加政治化。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, I do think our founders really had it right, that sometimes when you have overlapping jurisdiction, federal and state, and overlapping
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，我确实认为我们的开国元勋们是对的，有时候当你拥有重叠的管辖权，联邦和州，以及重叠的

sentences.en: branches of government between congressional investigations and executive branch investigations,
sentences.zh: 政府分支，介于国会调查和行政部门调查之间，

sentences.en: you actually do get at the right answer in the end, for reasons that James Madison said in Federalist 51, that people aren't angels.
sentences.zh: 你最终确实能得到正确的答案，原因正如詹姆斯·麦迪逊在《联邦党人文集》第51篇中所说，人不是天使。

sentences.en: And so if you can create overlapping investigative checks and balances, that it's going to be cumbersome, it's going to be frustrating,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能建立重叠的调查制衡机制，这会很繁琐，会很令人沮丧，

sentences.en: it's going to be slow, but it is the way that we get truth in our system.
sentences.zh: 会很缓慢，但这确实是我们系统中获得真相的方式。

sentences.en: Neil, I think listeners might hear that and think, oh, great, this has been a long, exhausting process, waiting for Mueller to finish this report.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，我想听众听到这些可能会想，哦，太棒了，等待穆勒完成这份报告已经是一个漫长而令人筋疲力尽的过程了。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you're saying, actually, this could really just be the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是在说，实际上，这可能才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: I know everyone in America wants a quick resolution to this.
sentences.zh: 我知道全美国的每个人都希望这件事能尽快解决。

sentences.en: I'm tired.
sentences.zh: 我累了。

sentences.en: Everyone's tired.
sentences.zh: 大家都累了。

sentences.en: But these are really hard investigations.
sentences.zh: 但这些调查确实非常艰难。

sentences.en: I mean, independent counsel investigations go on years after year under the old regime.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在旧体制下，独立检察官的调查持续了多年又多年。

sentences.en: I remember when I came in in 1998, we had an independent counsel from the Reagan administration that was still acting.
sentences.zh: 我记得1998年我刚加入时，我们还有一位来自里根政府时期的独立检察官仍在任职。

sentences.en: So this investigation in particular, because it involves counterintelligence and sources and methods and involves Russian documents and all sorts of people.
sentences.zh: 所以这次调查尤其如此，因为它涉及反间谍、情报来源和手段，还涉及俄罗斯文件以及各种各样的人。

sentences.en: It's amazing to think, actually, that in 19 months, there have been 37 indictments and 199 counts.
sentences.zh: 想到在19个月内就有37项起诉和199项指控，真是令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So I know that time delays are frustrating for everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道时间上的拖延让每个人都很沮丧。

sentences.en: But viewed in context, this has been one of the fastest investigations, not one of the sloweSt.
sentences.zh: 但放在背景中来看，这其实是最快的调查之一，而不是最慢的。

sentences.en: So Neil, having written the rules that will govern how this all plays out in response to the last two
sentences.zh: 那么尼尔，作为曾为应对前两次

sentences.en: big presidential investigations, do you suspect that when this is all over, we're going to have to rewrite these rules yet again?
sentences.zh: 重大总统调查而制定规则的人，你是否怀疑当这一切结束时，我们还得再次重写这些规则？

sentences.en: We just don't know yet because we're living in it right now.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道，因为我们正身处其中。

sentences.en: We don't know how the regulations have fared or not.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这些法规实施得如何。

sentences.en: We'll have to see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: And then we're going to have you on and we're going to ask you that question again.
sentences.zh: 到时候我们会再请你来，再问你这个问题。

sentences.en: I look forward to it.
sentences.zh: 我很期待。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks, Neil.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，尼尔。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: On Sunday, the chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, Jerry Nadler, said he would undertake
sentences.zh: 周日，众议院司法委员会主席杰里·纳德勒表示，他将进行

sentences.en: an investigation involving dozens of individuals and organizations connected to President Trump that could eventually lead to his impeachment.
sentences.zh: 一项涉及数十名与特朗普总统有关的个人和组织的调查，这最终可能导致对他的弹劾。

sentences.en: Do you think the president obstructed justice?
sentences.zh: 你认为总统妨碍了司法公正吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是。

sentences.en: It's very clear to the president obstructed justice.
sentences.zh: 总统妨碍司法公正这一点非常清楚。

sentences.en: It's very clear.
sentences.zh: 非常清楚。

sentences.en: 1,100 times he referred to the
sentences.zh: 他1100次将

sentences.en: Mueller investigation as a witch hunt.
sentences.zh: 穆勒调查称为“猎巫行动”。

sentences.en: He tried to protect Flynn from being investigated by the FBI.
sentences.zh: 他试图保护弗林免受联邦调查局的调查。

sentences.en: He fired Comey in order to stop the Russian thing, as he told NBC News.
sentences.zh: 正如他告诉NBC新闻的那样，他解雇科米是为了阻止“俄罗斯那档子事”。

sentences.en: He's intimidated witnesses in public.
sentences.zh: 他在公开场合恐吓证人。

sentences.en: If that's the case, then is the decision not to pursue impeachment right now simply political?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，那么现在决定不进行弹劾仅仅是出于政治考虑吗？

sentences.en: In an interview with ABC's This Week, Nadler said he has made no determination about whether to proceed
sentences.zh: 在接受美国广播公司《本周》节目采访时，纳德勒表示他尚未决定是否推进

sentences.en: with impeachment, but said he is convinced that the president obstructed justice, the same charge
sentences.zh: 弹劾，但他表示确信总统妨碍了司法公正，这与国会对尼克松总统和克林顿总统提出的指控相同，

sentences.en: brought by Congress against President Nixon and President Clinton, following independent council investigations into both.
sentences.zh: 这两次指控都是在独立检察官调查之后提出的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: In a major setback for President Trump, a Republican ally in the Senate, Rand Paul of Kentucky, says he will support a resolution
sentences.zh: 在特朗普总统遭遇重大挫折之际，参议院的一位共和党盟友、来自肯塔基州的兰德·保罗表示，他将支持一项决议，

sentences.en: blocking Trump's declaration of a national emergency, calling it an illegal way to build a border wall without the approval of Congress.
sentences.zh: 阻止特朗普宣布国家紧急状态，称这是在未经国会批准的情况下修建边境墙的非法手段。

sentences.en: Paul's support for the resolution, which has already passed in the democratically controlled House, makes him the fourth Republican senator to back the measure,
sentences.zh: 保罗对该决议的支持——该决议已在民主党控制的众议院获得通过——使他成为第四位支持该措施的共和党参议员，

sentences.en: and now puts the resolution on track to pass in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 现在该决议有望在参议院获得通过。

sentences.en: In a speech over the weekend,
sentences.zh: 在周末的一次演讲中，

sentences.en: Paul said, quote, I can't vote to give the president the power to spend money that hasn't been approved by Congress.
sentences.zh: 保罗说：“我不能投票授权总统花费未经国会批准的资金。”

sentences.en: If, as expected, the resolution passes in the Senate, it will likely force Trump to issue the first veto of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 如果该决议如预期般在参议院获得通过，它很可能会迫使特朗普动用他总统任期内的首次否决权。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Marlboro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·马尔伯勒。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
